note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute gastroenteritis-like illness with profuse watery diarrhoea and crampy abdominal pain; associated nausea and vomiting (milk-triggered); feverish sensation.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began about three days ago; diarrhoea is persistent and otherwise not improving; stools described as very watery with near-hourly frequency when awake.
- Context/triggers: Diarrhoea started after Monday/Tuesday; brother has had a similar illness for five days; no clear food trigger identified.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea; one episode of vomiting after milk intake; feeling hot/febrile; reduced sleep; urinary frequency reportedly decreased but still present.
- Diet/fluid intake: Drinking water but feels fluids are passing through; last solid intake at lunch today; overall fluid loss significant.
- Social and work: Works in government office in Central London; attempts to continue work;smoking socially; occasional alcohol use.
- PMH/medications/allergies: Patient reports being fit and well with no regular medications; takes occasional paracetamol; no known drug allergies.
- Family history: Father has colon cancer (stage unclear); patient’s father is currently affected.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: None reported; deemed fit and well.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Medications: Occasional paracetamol; no regular medications.

Physical Examination:
- No formal vital signs or physical exam findings documented in transcript.
- Patient-reported symptoms include feverish sensation and abdominal pain; no reported blood in stool.

Impression:
- Gastroenteritis (acute infectious gastroenteritis) suspected.

Management Plan:
- Hydration: Advise maintaining high fluid intake; recommend oral rehydration solution (Diarolyte) to replace fluids and minerals (dose/amount not documented).
- Diet: Clear fluids first; introduce soft diet (e.g., soup, mashed foods) as tolerated; gradually advance as able.
- Medications: Paracetamol as needed for fever/pain (dose/route/frequency not documented); avoid alcohol.
- Monitoring: If symptoms do not settle within 48 hours or signs of dehydration develop, contact clinician for further evaluation.
- Follow-up: Reassess in 1–2 days; call back sooner if dehydration, fever worsening, or inability to keep fluids down.

Patient Summary:
- The patient presents with an approximately 3-day history of acute watery diarrhoea with crampy lower abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, plus feverish sensations. The presentation is compatible with gastroenteritis. Plan includes hydration with an oral rehydration solution (Diarolyte), a soft/adequate diet, and acetaminophen as needed; a check-in is planned in 1–2 days with instructions to seek earlier care if dehydration or symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Stay well hydrated with oral rehydration solution (Diarolyte) or clear fluids; avoid dehydration.
- Use paracetamol for fever/pain as needed.
- If no improvement or dehydration signs within 48 hours, contact the clinician for further assessment.

Next Steps:
- Monitor hydration status and tolerance of fluids/foods.
- No prescription required for Diarolyte; continue simple fluids and gradual dietary advancement.
- Follow up in 1–2 days or sooner if dehydration, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, or worsening symptoms.
